## 1. Identity

- Module name: `py_soc`
- Library category: `cpu`
- Location: `ip/cpu/py_soc/`
- One-line purpose: Python microcontroller. py_core plus code/constant memory, a flash boot loader, an AXI4-Lite interconnect and the library peripherals: SPI NOR flash controller, 2x UART, 2x I2C master, 2x SPI master, 
- Version: 1.0.0

## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Python microcontroller. py_core plus code/constant memory,
a flash boot loader, an AXI4-Lite interconnect and the library
peripherals: SPI NOR flash controller, 2x UART, 2x I2C master, 2x SPI
master, 3x 32-bit GPIO, watchdog and interrupt controller. Every
streaming data path (UART, I2C, SPI, flash) goes through a
py_stream_port with its own TX and RX FIFO (*_TX_FIFO / *_RX_FIFO
words, default 16), so receive can be polled (RXDATA valid bit) or
interrupt driven (IRQ_EN).
Every peripheral instance has its own parameter set: UART0 / UART1
(*_BAUD, *_TX_FIFO, *_RX_FIFO), I2C0 / I2C1 (*_HZ, FIFOs), SPI0 / SPI1
(*_HZ, *_DATA_W, FIFOs), FLASH (FLASH_CLKDIV, FIFOs). The shared
UART_BAUD, I2C_HZ, SPI_HZ and *_TX/RX_FIFO parameters are the defaults
of both instances of a kind.

Boot - on every release of reset (rst_n or watchdog) py_boot owns the
bus, copies the pyc.py image from flash address BOOT_ADDR into code and
constant memory, checks it, and starts the core at pc 0. boot_done_o /
boot_err_o / boot_err_code_o report the result; a bad image leaves the
core stopped. After boot the core owns the bus, and the flash stays
available to software (e.g. data logging) at 0xC000.

Address map (src/py_soc_map_pkg.sv, read by the decoder below, the
testbenches and the firmware; each window 256 bytes; *_D =
py_stream_port data port):
  0x0100 SYSCTL (reset cause, boot status, cycle counter, ID, CORE_RESET)
  0x1000 INTC   0x2000 WDT    0x3000 GPIO0  0x4000 GPIO1  0x5000 GPIO2
  0x6000 UART0  0x6100 UART0_D  0x7000 UART1  0x7100 UART1_D
  0x8000 I2C0   0x8100 I2C0_D   0x9000 I2C1   0x9100 I2C1_D
  0xA000 SPI0   0xA100 SPI0_D   0xB000 SPI1   0xB100 SPI1_D
  0xC000 FLASH  0xC100 FLASH_D
  0x1_0000-0x1_FFFF EXT (EXT_EN = 1): the m_ext_axil_* master port, for
                    registers outside py_soc (address offset in the window)
Unmapped addresses return DECERR (core trap TRAP_BUS).

Core logic reset - core_rst_n_o follows SYSCTL CORE_RESET[0] (0x0120):
low from every system reset until the firmware writes 1, so the logic
outside py_soc (e.g. a video datapath) stays in reset until the CPU has
booted and tested itself. Synchronous to clk; synchronise it per clock
domain (reset_sync) where it is used.

Interrupt controller sources (all level):
  0 UART0_D  1 UART1_D  2 I2C0_D  3 I2C1_D  4 SPI0_D  5 SPI1_D
  6 GPIO0    7 GPIO1    8 GPIO2   9 WDT pre-timeout
  10 FLASH command done  11 FLASH_D
  12-15 ext_irq_i[3:0] (level, synchronous to clk; tie low if unused)

Reset - rst_n (synchronous, active low) resets everything. A watchdog
expiry is stretched to WDT_RST_CYCLES clocks (wdt_reset_o) and resets
the whole system, watchdog included, so it comes back disabled like
any other reset; the system then boots from flash again. Clock - clk
only.

Clock generator (CLKGEN_EN = 1) - clk is then the reference clock
(REF_KHZ) and rst_n an asynchronous reset. clk_gen (ip/clock/clk_gen,
two all-digital PLLs) makes the CPU clock REF_KHZ * CPU_M / (CPU_D *
CPU_O), a clock multiplier, which runs everything in py_soc (cpu_clk_o),
and NCLK further clocks clk_o[n] = CPU clock * CLK_M / (CLK_D *
CLK_O[n]), phase aligned with each other. The system stays in reset
until the CPU loop is locked (cpu_rst_n_o, synchronous to cpu_clk_o,
for logic outside py_soc in the CPU clock domain). SYSCTL CLK_EN
(0x0124) gates each clk_o[n] (reset value CLK_EN_RST), CLK_STATUS
(0x0128) bit 0 shows the output loop locked, and core_rst_n_o is only
released while it is (CORE_RESET AND locked, registered), so the core
logic reset keeps a single source. With CLKGEN_EN = 0 (default) clk is
the CPU clock, cpu_clk_o = clk, cpu_rst_n_o = rst_n, clk_o = 0. CLK_HZ
is the CPU clock frequency in both cases (checked against the clock
generator setting to 100 ppm). Defaults: CLKGEN_EN = 1, 33.333 MHz
reference, CPU 200 MHz (x24 / 4), one 100 MHz output (x4 / 8); UART
115200 baud, I2C 400 kHz, SPI 10 MHz, boot flash 33 MHz. For synthesis only the PLL oscillators
(dpll_dco) are black boxes; see clk_gen.sv.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys (through sv2v: add the `scripts/sv2v` marker file).
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 8111 LUTs, 8787 flip-flops, 1 DSP48E1, 2 RAMB36E1, 1 RAMB18E1. Stay within about this budget.

## 8. File header

Read the file header template from `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt` and start every file you create (RTL, testbench, test tasks, scripts, file lists, Makefile) with that header, filled in: Filename, Author: FPGA Cores 4 U, Description, Date. In RTL the Description is the specification (behaviour, register map, parameters, clocks, resets, clock-domain crossings, latency, resources, errors); in testbenches it says what is checked; test-task files list every task with a one-line description (the test list scripts use it).

Header template file: `ip/docs/HEADER_TEMPLATE.txt`   (replace with your own template file if needed)

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
System testbench for py_soc running tb/programs/selftest.py
(compiled by py_core/tools/pyc.py into a flash image; see
scripts/run_test.sh). The image is loaded into a behavioral SPI NOR
flash model and the SoC boots from it. Board wiring - the flash on the
boot SPI pins, UART0 TXD -> UART1 RXD and back, each SPI MOSI -> its MISO,
I2C0 to a slave model at 0x50 and I2C1 to one at 0x51, GPIO0 pads
looped to GPIO1 inputs, GPIO2 inputs driven here. The testbench pulses
GPIO2 pins 0 and 31 when the firmware reaches stage 2, then waits for
the watchdog reset, checks the firmware's result globals at that
moment, and checks that the system boots from flash again and the
firmware halts reporting the watchdog as the reset cause. The core
logic reset output (core_rst_n_o) must be held after reset, released by
the firmware's SYSCTL CORE_RESET write, and held again by the watchdog
reset. Any core
trap fails the test. With +corrupt one payload byte of the image is
flipped and the test instead expects boot_err (checksum) and a core
that never starts. Prints TEST PASSED on success.
The test tasks are in tests/py_soc_tests.sv (`included).
```

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh py_soc --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `py_soc_tb` | `py_soc_tb` | one test: System testbench for py_soc running tb/programs/selftest.py (compiled by py_core/tools/pyc.py into a flash image; see scripts/run_test.sh). |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C cpu/py_soc test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.
